quizzes.title: Quiz on Video: Transition Words
quizzes.lesson: Lesson 14: Using Transition Words and Phrases

questions.question: A transition can be used for which of the following reasons?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
d)
All of the above
Explanation
:
A transition is used to make connections between ideas in writing. Some types of connections are expressing agreement, indicating addition, and indicating opposition.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a transitional word that expresses opposition?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) Never
Explanation:
“Although”, “but”, and “yet” are examples of transition words that express opposition. “Never” is not normally used as a transitional word.

questions.question: How do transitions help improve your writing?
options: By helping avoid confusion for the reader.
By making ideas flow better between sentences or paragraphs.
By creating connections between ideas in writing
questions.explanation:
Answer:
d) All of the above
Explanation:
Transitions create connections between ideas in writing. Using transitions also improves your writing by helping avoid confusion for the reader and by making your ideas flow better.

quizzes.title: Final Quiz: Transition Words and Phrases
quizzes.lesson: Lesson 14: Using Transition Words and Phrases

questions.question: Where is the best place for a transition between paragraphs?
options: the last sentence of the first of two paragraphs
the first sentence of the first of two paragraphs
the first sentence of the second of two paragraphs
in a single sentence between two paragraphs
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c)
Explanation:
The best place for a transition between paragraphs is typically
c) the first sentence of the second of two paragraphs
. This allows you to smoothly introduce the new idea or topic while linking it to the previous paragraph.
However, depending on the context, using
d) a single sentence between two paragraphs
can also be effective for more complex transitions.

questions.question:
German Shepherd Dogs
(adapted from Dogtime.com
)
If you’re buying a puppy, you’ll get a slightly different kind of German Shepherd depending on whether you choose an American versus a German breeder. _______________ American breeders are often aiming to create dog show champions, and they breed puppies more for that distinctive German Shepherd look than for those distinctive German Shepherd talents.
Question: Which is the best transitional phrase to go in the blank space above?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b)
Explanation:
The best transitional phrase to go in the blank space is
“For example,”
because it introduces a specific instance that illustrates the point made in the first sentence about the differences between American and German breeders. “Instead” would imply a contrast, which doesn’t fit here, and “However” suggests a contradiction that isn’t present in the context.

questions.question:
German Shepherd Dogs
(adapted from Dogtime.com
)
If you’re buying a puppy, you’ll get a slightly different kind of German Shepherd depending on whether you choose an American versus a German breeder. For example
,
American breeders are often aiming to create dog show champions, and they breed puppies more for that distinctive German Shepherd look than for those distinctive German Shepherd talents.
Fans say that American-bred German Shepherds are calmer than their German counterparts, but critics say these dogs have lost some of their talents for working traditional German Shepherd jobs, and are more prone to behavior problems such as separation anxiety.
{____________________________________________________________ }
Before a German Shepherd is bred in Germany, he has to pass numerous tests to prove he measures up to the physical and mental benchmarks the breed is known for. German Shepherd dogs from Germany tend to have a more energetic and driven personality.
Which is the best transitional sentence to go in the blank space above?
options: German Shepherds in Germany work hard, however.
German breeders, on the other hand, breed German Shepherds for their working abilities.
German breeders breed German Shepherds for their working abilities.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b)
Explanation:
The best transitional sentence to go in the blank space is b)
German breeders, on the other hand, breed German Shepherds for their working abilities
. This sentence effectively contrasts with the previous sentence about American-bred German Shepherds and sets up the discussion about the breeding practices in Germany. It clearly highlights the difference in focus between the two breeding styles.

questions.question:
“I know more than my sister. I’m twelve years older than her. She hasn’t started school yet.”
By adding one or two transition in the sentence mentioned above, we can see again how the parts relate to each other.
QUESTION: Which of the following options includes transitions that help you understand?
options: I know more than my sister because I’m twelve years older than her, and she hasn’t started school yet."
I know more than my sister. However, I’m twelve years older than her. She hasn’t started school yet.
I know more than my sister. I’m twelve years older than her, sometimes she hasn’t started school yet.
I know more than my sister. I’m twelve years older than her, sometimes she hasn’t started school yet.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
a)
Explanation:
The best option that includes a transition to help understand the relationships between the parts is
“
“I know more than my sister because I’m twelve years older than her, and she hasn’t started school yet.”
This version clearly explains the cause-and-effect relationship, making it easy to see why the speaker knows more. The transitions phrases (“and” & “because”) clarify the relationship between the speaker’s age, the sister’s schooling, and the knowledge difference.

questions.question:
DIRECTIONS: Read the following stimulus material
“Tweens” Are Ready for Cell Phones
A speech by Deborah Pendergast at the Safer Kids Summit
Thank you for inviting me to the first “Safer Kids Summit.” We are here to discuss ways to keep our children safe in an increasingly complex world. Today’s focus is on technology — specifically on the ideal age to give kids their own cell phones. As a representative of a large telecommunications company, I receive many inquiries from parents on this topic, and this is what I tell them: It depends on the child, of course, but in general, age 10 is just about right.
A 2012 survey by the National Consumers League backs me up. The survey found that almost 60 percent of children ages 8 to 12 already have cell phones. These “tweens” can contact their parents at any time, and vice versa, giving the kids a sense of empowerment and their parents a feeling of security. Caroline Knorr, of the group Common Sense Media, says, “We want our kids to be independent, to be able to walk home from school and play at the playground without us. We want them to have that old-fashioned, fun experience of being on their own, and cell phones can help with that.” Picture the following scenario: You told your fourth-grader that you would pick her up after school, but you are stuck in traffic. She is waiting for you …and waiting, and waiting. But if you both have cell phones, you can call her to let her know you are delayed, and she can go back inside the school, where there are adults around. You both breathe a sigh of relief.
Psychologists tell us that the period between ages 10 and 12 is one of growing independence. It is a time to teach children about responsibility, and to give them opportunities to earn our trust. Providing a 10-year-old with a cell phone offers an ideal way to achieve these goals and gives parents peace of mind as well.
QUESTION: What is the main argument, or point?
options: Almost 60 percent of children ages 8 to 12 already have cell phones.
Tweens are not ready for cell phones.
Tweens are children in between elementary school and teenagers.
Cell phones can help tweens learn to be safe.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
d) Cell phones can help tweens learn to be safe.
Explanation:
The speaker emphasizes how cell phones provide a sense of security for both children and their parents, as well as opportunities for tweens to learn responsibility and independence.

Source Material #1
“Tweens” Are Ready for Cell Phones
A speech by Deborah Pendergast at the Safer Kids Summit
Thank you for inviting me to the first “Safer Kids Summit.” We are here to discuss ways to keep our children safe in an increasingly complex world. Today’s focus is on technology — specifically on the ideal age to give kids their own cell phones. As a representative of a large telecommunications company, I receive many inquiries from parents on this topic, and this is what I tell them: It depends on the child, of course, but in general, age 10 is just about right.
A 2012 survey by the National Consumers League backs me up. The survey found that almost 60 percent of children ages 8 to 12 already have cell phones. These “tweens” can contact their parents at any time, and vice versa, giving the kids a sense of empowerment and their parents a feeling of security. Caroline Knorr, of the group Common Sense Media, says, “We want our kids to be independent, to be able to walk home from school and play at the playground without us. We want them to have that old-fashioned, fun experience of being on their own, and cell phones can help with that.” Picture the following scenario: You told your fourth-grader that you would pick her up after school, but you are stuck in traffic. She is waiting for you …and waiting, and waiting. But if you both have cell phones, you can call her to let her know you are delayed, and she can go back inside the school, where there are adults around. You both breathe a sigh of relief.
Psychologists tell us that the period between ages 10 and 12 is one of growing independence. It is a time to teach children about responsibility, and to give them opportunities to earn our trust. Providing a 10-year-old with a cell phone offers an ideal way to achieve these goals and gives parents peace of mind as well.
Source Material #2
Wait Until They Are Older
A speech by Linda Sidner  at the Safer Kids Summit
Good morning! I come to this topic as a parent and a veteran teacher of so-called “tweens.” I love kids this age for their curiosity and energy, but those same qualities can lead to trouble if not overseen by adults. That’s why giving children their own phones actually makes them less safe, not more. I believe that the best age for a cell phone is 16, the point at which we consider kids grown-up enough to learn to drive — and even then, parents must set firm limits on phone use!
Why are tweens with phones less safe? For one thing, parents may be lulled into a false sense of security if their kids have phones. They may become careless about knowing where their child is and who he is with, thinking, “I can always reach him on his phone.” For another, cell phones give children access to all the frightening, dangerous, and inappropriate sites on the internet, with no parent nearby to monitor this activity.
But perhaps the most worrisome aspect of giving cell phones to children is the rise in “cyberbullying” or “text bullying.” Text bullying means using a cell phone to send cruel, embarrassing, or false text messages to or about someone. In one study, researcher Elizabeth Englander found that by middle school, over 90% of children report that they use their cell phones to text or go onto the internet. She also found that in grades 3 through 5, between 14 and 19 percent of children reported being victims of cyberbullying. What if it’s your child on the receiving end of this cruelty? Or, perhaps worse, what if your child is the bully? Children of this age are simply not mature enough to handle this technology, and we shouldn’t expect them to be. It’s our job as adults to protect them. That’s why I say: It’s better to wait.

: Analyze the arguments presented in the two speeches. Which position has more evidence than the other? Explain how one position is better supported than the other. Incorporate relevant and specific evidence from both sources to support your argument. Remember, the better-argued position is not necessarily the position that you agree with.
options: The first statement has better evidence.
Children should get phones at age 10 because it can help teach them about responsibility.
Linda Sidner supports her arguments on the amount of cyberbullying with scientific evidence and argues her point better than Deborah Pendergast.
Deborah Pendergast is a telecommunications representative and knows what she is talking about.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) Linda Sinder supports her arguments no the amount of cyberbullying with scientific evidence and argues her point better than Deborah Pendergast
Explanation:
Linda Sidner presents concrete data, including statistics on cyberbullying, to support her argument that children are not mature enough to handle cell phones safely. This use of scientific research makes her argument stronger compared to Deborah Pendergast, whose claims rely on general statements about independence and parental convenience, but lack specific evidence. Sidner’s argument is better supported because it is grounded in research and addresses the potential dangers associated with giving tweens cell phones.

questions.question:
DIRECTIONS: Read the following stimulus material.
Parenting Education Should Be Mandatory
By Kai Fernandez, APRN, the
Freeport Times
As a nurse practitioner in a pediatric office, I had to complete extensive training and obtain a license before I could examine my first toddler. Many jobs, from barber to pilot, involve specific training. But for the most important job — raising children to be responsible adults —no training is required, and children and society suffer the results of this lack of knowledge. The time has come to correct this situation. Before they can be discharged from the hospital, first-time parents should be required to take parenting classes.
Just as we equip new drivers with a learner’s permit and instruction, we must also equip new parents with the skills they need. While some people might believe that this is the “nanny state” stepping on the rights of individuals, I am not suggesting that there is only one “correct” style of parenting. But there is basic information about infants and children that every parent should be required to know, including nutrition, health and safety, and stages of child development. Knowing how to safely bathe a baby, for example, would prevent many tragedies. Understanding that babies are crying to communicate, not to be “naughty,” helps parents adjust their expectations and their behavior.
And parent education works. According to the Centers for Disease Control, for example, the “Safe To Sleep” campaign has reduced the number of deaths from Sudden Infant Death Syndrome by fifty percent since 1994 just by teaching parents to put babies to bed on their backs. Conversely, uninformed parenting hurts not only children, but the rest of us as well. A study by the Department of Education in England found that children whose parents use harsh or inconsistent discipline are more likely to have poor attention spans, low levels of literacy, and antisocial behavior.
In cultures where extended families are the rule, raising children is a group effort. But in the modern world, new parents are on their own. It is our obligation as a society to make sure they have the skills to do their best in this challenging job. Making parenting classes mandatory is a step towards this goal.
QUESTION: What is the main argument, or point?
options: I had to complete extensive training and obtain a license before I could examine my first toddler.
First-time parents should be required to take parenting classes.
Understanding that babies are crying to communicate, not to be “naughty,” helps parents adjust their expectations and their behavior.
Raising children is a group effort.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b) First-time parents should be required to take parenting classes.
Explanation:
The author emphasizes that parenting education should be mandatory for first-time parents to ensure they are equipped with essential skills and knowledge, which can benefit both children and society.

questions.question:
A violent storm has threatened the first voyage of the ship
Nan-Shan
. This excerpt from a work of fiction portrays several crew members, including the first mate, Jukes, as they confront the storm.
Para. 1
Jukes was as ready a man as any half-dozen young mates that may be caught by casting a net upon the waters; and though he had been somewhat taken aback by the startling viciousness of the first squall, he had pulled himself together on the instant, had called out the hands, and had rushed them along to secure such openings about the deck as had not been already battened down earlier in the evening. Shouting in his fresh, stentorian voice, “Jump, boys, and bear a hand!” he led in the work, telling himself the while that he had “just expected this.”
Para. 2
But at the same time he was growing aware that this was rather more than he had expected. From the first stir of the air felt on his cheek the gale seemed to take upon itself the accumulated impetus of an avalanche. Heavy sprays enveloped the
Nan-Shan
from stem to stern, and instantly in the midst of her regular rolling she began to jerk and plunge as though she had gone mad with fright.
Para. 3
Jukes thought, “This is no joke. ”While he was exchanging explanatory yells with his captain, a sudden lowering of the darkness came upon the night, falling before their vision like something palpable. It was as if the masked lights of the world had been turned down. Jukes was uncritically glad to have his captain at hand. It relieved him as though that man had, by simply coming on deck, taken most of the gale’s weight upon his shoulders. Such is the prestige, the privilege, and the burden of command.
Para. 4
Captain MacWhirr could expect no relief of that sort from anyone on earth. Such is the loneliness of command. He was trying to see, with that watchful manner of a seaman who stares into the wind’s eye as if into the eye of an adversary, to penetrate the hidden intention and guess the aim and force of the thrust. The strong wind swept at him out of a vast obscurity; he felt under his feet the uneasiness of his ship, and he could not even discern the shadow of her shape. He wished it were not so; and very still he waited . . .
QUESTION: In paragraph 1, the description of Jukes as “
as ready a man as any half-dozen young mates that may be caught by casting a net upon the waters
” means that he:
options: is better at fishing than other men on his ship.
is a good catch because he has had many years of experience.
is as generally capable as other first mates.
does the work of six men.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) is a generally capable as other first mates
Explanation:
The description compares Jukes to other first mates, implying that he is just as competent and capable as any typical young mate, not that he has more experience or does the work of multiple men.

DIRECTIONS: Read the following job application letter, and then answer a question about the numbered sentences in the letter. Choose the answer that would result in the most effective writing of the sentence or sentences.
Jonathan Quinn,
Employment Director,
Capital City Gardening Services,
4120 Wisconsin Avenue, N.W.
Washington, DC 20036
Dear Mr. Quinn:
(1) I would like to apply for the landscape supervisor position advertised in the Sunday, April 30th, edition of the
Washington Post
.
(2) My work experience and education, combined with your need for an experienced landscape supervisor, has resulted in a relationship that would profit both parties.
(3) In May, I graduated from Prince William Community College.
(4) Graduating with an Associate of Arts Degree in horticulture.
(5) My focus within the program which was designing gardens and choosing the plants for particular soils and regions.
(6) I have also had considerable experience in supervising.
(7) For several years, while  with the local company Burke Nursery and Garden Center, and had been responsible for supervising the four members of the planting staff.
(8) Our community knows Capital City Gardening Services is a company that does excellent work.
(9) It strives hard to meet the demands of it’s clients.
(10) As my references will attest, I am a diligent worker and have the respect of both my coworkers and my customers.
(11) I will be, as a landscape supervisor at your firm, able to put to use the skills and knowledge that I have obtained and continue the tradition you have established.
(12) I have included a copy of my resume detailing my principal interests education, and past work experience.
(13) Photographs of the landscape projects I have supervised as well as drawings of proposed projects are also included.
(14) The opportunities that this position provides and the many challenges that this position provides are things that I am excited about in regards to this position.
(15) Thank you for your consideration, I look forward to hearing from you.
Sincerely,
Patrick Omer
QUESTION:  Which sentence below would be most effective if it was added before sentence 8?
options: There are many companies in this community and Capital City Gardening Services is one of them.
As a resident of Capital City, I am very familiar with many of your public projects.
Like carpet-cleaning services, gardening services range in cost.
Gosh, I don’t know where to begin when saying good things about your company.
questions.explanation:

b) As a resident of Capital City, I am very familiar with many of your public projects.
Explanation:
This sentence strengthens the writer’s connection to the company and shows familiarity with its work, making it a relevant and professional transition into the praise for Capital City Gardening Services in sentence 8.

questions.question:
Adapted from the TASC reading test practice
DIRECTIONS: Read the text and then answer the question.
How to Shop Safely Online
What is the best way to save parking charges and avoid crowds at the mall? You can shop online. More and more consumers are finding online shopping the most convenient way to make purchases. In 2010, online sales on the day after Thanksgiving were 15.9 percent higher than they were in 2009. New technology even makes it possible to shop from mobile devices. However, there is a downside to this new and easy shopping access. Not every online site is safe from hackers, and some sites deliberately try to mislead consumers.
Some websites use web addresses that are formatted to look almost the same as legitimate sites. This tactic is called spoofing. The site may also use icons and trademarks similar to those on safe sites. A spoofed website often engages in another illegitimate activity called phishing. The object of phishing is to obtain credit card, bank account, or Social Security numbers from an unsuspecting consumer. On one of these sites, you might believe you are charging a pair of hiking boots, when you are actually providing some stranger with the information needed to book a flight to Acapulco on your credit card.
There are some common sense ways to recognize a spoofed site. Check the web address carefully to make sure the domain name is in bold type. Make sure there are no typographical errors in the name. Spoofers often use a name that is just a few letters different from a legitimate site. Pay careful attention to any warnings from your web browser saying that a site is potentially unsafe. Keep your browser updated so you have the latest available protection.
QUESTION: Which of the following quotes from the text does not offer evidence of the dangers of online shopping?
options: The site may also use icons and trademarks similar to those on safe sites.

On one of these sites, you might believe you are charging a pair of hiking boots, when you are actually providing some stranger with the information needed to book a flight to Acapulco on your credit card.
Some websites use web addresses that are formatted to look almost the same as legitimate sites.
However, there is a downside to this new and easy shopping access.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
d) However, there is a downside to this new and easy shopping access
Explanation:
The question asks, which one of the quotes does NOT offer evidence of the dangers of online shopping? The first three all offer an example of  how spoof websites cheat online shoppers. The last quote does not offer supporting evidence – it just states that online shopping has a downside.
Always make sure you understand what the question is asking.

options: Convert the fractions to improper numbers.

Explanation:
When the denominators are the same, it is simple to add or subtract the numerators from one another just as you would if they were integers. To add ⅕ to ⅖ you will simply add the numerators 1 + 2 = 3.
Therefore the answer to ⅕ + ⅖ is ⅗.
The denominator will stay the same.

questions.question: What should you do when adding or subtracting fractions if the denominators are different?
options: Use the smallest of the denominators.
Use the largest of the denominators.
You must first change one of the fractions so that both fractions have the same denominator.
questions.explanation:

d) Change one of the fractions so that both fractions have the same denominator.
Explanation:
In order to add or subtract fractions, the denominators have to be the same. So, you need to first change one of the fractions so that the denominators match.

questions.question: When adding two fractions with different denominators, what is the best way to start?
options: List multiples of the largest denominator until you find the first one that can be evenly divided by the other denominator.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b)
Start with the largest of the two denominators to find the least common multiple.
Explanation
:
It is easiest to start with the largest denominator. You will list its multiples until you find one that can be evenly divided by the other denominator. In the example of 1/10 and 1/3 you would try:
1 x 10 = 10. NO you cannot divide 10 / 3 and get a whole number.
2 x 10 = 20. NO you cannot divide 20 / 3 and get a whole number.
3 x 10 = 30. YES 30 / 3 a whole number. In this example 30 is your lowest common denominator.

questions.question:
What is the lowest (least) common denominator between
3/5
and
6/7
?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
a) 35
Explanation:
35 is the lowest whole number that can be divided evenly by both 7 and 5. To find the lowest common denominator you can list the multiples of each number until you find the first in common.
Following is a step-by-step explanation:
Identify the denominators
: Look at the fractions and identify their denominators. In this case, the denominators are 5 and 7 for the fractions 3/5 and 6/7 respectively.
Find the multiples of each denominator
: Start by listing out the multiples of each denominator until you find a common multiple.
For 5: Multiples are 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, …
For 7: Multiples are 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, …
Identify the least common multiple (LCM)
: Look for the smallest number that appears in both lists. This is the least common multiple (LCM) of the two denominators.
In this case, you can see that 35 is the smallest number that appears in both lists, so LCM(5, 7) = 35.
The LCM is the lowest common denominator (LCD)
: Since the LCM is the smallest number that both denominators divide into evenly, it is also the lowest common denominator (LCD) of the fractions.
So, by finding the LCM of 5 and 7, we found that the lowest common denominator between 3/5 and 6/7 is
35.

questions.question:
How would you rewrite the equation
3/5 + 4/7
using the lowest common denominator?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c)
21/35 + 20/35
Explanation:
First you find the lowest common denominator of 5 and 7 which is 35. Then you see how many times each denominator goes into 35.
35 / 5 = 7 and 35 / 7 = 5.
Next you multiply the numerator by the same number.
7 x 3 = 21 and 5 x 4 = 20.
Your new equation is 21/35 + 20/35

At the beginning of the season, Tomas had to remove 5 orange trees from his farm. Each of the remaining trees produced 210 oranges for a total harvest of 41,790 oranges.

Answer: c)

We need to make an equation to find the original number of trees. Let t be the original number of trees – it is the variable you need to find.
Tomas has t – 5 trees and they produced 210 oranges. So (t – 5) multiplied by 210 is equal to the total number of oranges, which we know is 41,790.

210(t – 5) = 41,790
210(t – 5)/210 = 41,790/210 (use calculator here)

questions.question:
Factor
{$x^{2}$}+7x+12
.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b)
Explanation:
It’s easier to multiply polynomials than factor polynomials. So use
backsolving
for this question.
The first term is x2, so we know that the factors will both start with x to look like this: (x + __)(x + __) because that’s the only combination that would give us x2 in the answer. So we can ignore the two answers that don’t start that way.
Let’s start by
backsolving
the other two answers:
We’ll multiply all the parts of (x + 3)(x + 4) :
x multiplied by x = (x)(x) = x2
x multiplied by 4 = (x)(4) = 4x
3 multiplied by x = (3)(x) = 3x
3 multiplied by 4 = (3)(4) = 12
Put them together: {$x^{2}$} + 4x + 3x + 12 is the same as
{$x^{2}$} + 7x + 12 = (x+3)(x+4)
So we “back–solved” or work in reverse, to solve the question with our first try! If that hadn’t worked, we would have kept going and multiplied another answer choice, but we didn’t need to in this case.

V = (length)(width)(height)= lwh
.  We need to find the volume of the box and the volume of the eraser to answer the question.
Keeping in mind the final answer is the volume of the art box minus the volume of the eraser.
First let’s find the volume of the art box. The box is 5 inches by 8 inches by 2 inches. So the volume is 5 x 8 x 2 = 80 cubic inches.
Now let’s find how much of that volume is taken up by the eraser. The eraser is 2 inches by 1 inch by 0.25 of an inch. So the volume of the eraser is  2 x 1 x 0.25 = 0.5 cubic inches.

V = 4/3 x 3.14 x {$7.5^{3}$}

The width of the container will be 3 inches.

Answer: c)
Explanation:
This is a good question for working in reverse, because you have the formula and possible answers. The formula has to work for every pair to be the right answer. So you can replace x with the numbers in the input set and see if you get the paired number in the output.
Look at the first answer f(x)= x+ 8 using x =1: 1 + 8 = 9, not 12, as the table shows. So that answer is wrong. No need to check another point, move on to the next answer.
Look at the second answer f(x) = x+12 using x = 1: 1 + 12 = 13, not 12, so that answer is wrong too. Move on quickly to the next answer.
Look at the third answer f(x) = 5x+7 using x = 1: 5(1)+ 7 = 12, so that works. Try a second point to verify using x – 3. And 5(3)+ 7 = 22 works as well.
If you function f(x) = 5x + 7 with the last two pairs, you will see that it works for 5 and 10, too. You don’t need to go any further.
Katrina’s function is f(x) = 5x+ 7.

questions.question:
Menhet has a weekend job as a soccer referee. One weekend she earns $140 by working 4 games. Another weekend she earns $210 from working 6 games.
If Menhet graphed the equation to represent her total earnings based on the number of games, what would be the slope of the graph?
Use the formula:
{$\Large m=\frac{y_{2}-y_{1}}{x_{2}-x_{1}}$}
questions.explanation:
Answer: b)
Explanation:
From Mehnet’s story, we get the pairs (4, 140) and (6, 210).
First let’s make sure we know which is which.
First pair is (4, 140). So x1 =4 and y1 =140.
Second pair as (6, 210). So x2 =6 and y2 =210.
Next, we put them into the equation.
m = (210 – 140) ÷ (6 – 4) = 70/2 = 35
The slope is 35.

questions.question: In the set of numbers 1, 5, 5, 6, 8, what does the number 5 represent?
questions.explanation:
Answer:

Factory A

questions.explanation:
Answer: a)
Explanation:
To get the average increase, you can simply divide it among the five workers. An increase of $15 in the total daily wages of the workers divided equally by the 5 workers results in the average increasing by $3.

140 + 160 + 200 + 190 + 180 = 870. $870/5 = $174 average

The increase in the average wage for Factory A is $3.

We know it’s going to be seven times something so we can eliminate the first and last choices and focus on the two middle choices. But is it 7n + 4 or 7(n + 4)? The clue is in the word sum.
The sum is the total of numbers added together, so 7 times the sum means 7 times both n and 4 together. 7n + 4 would be written seven times n and four. But 7(n + 4) shows us that 7 applies to the sum of n + 4; so, that’s the right expression.

The correct answer is A.

5 rolls of quarters, 6 rolls of dimes
6 rolls of quarters, 5 rolls of dimes
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b) 7 rolls of quarters, 4 rolls of dimes
Explanation:
This is a good question for back–solving.
It will be quicker to test each answer than to set up an equation and do the calculations. Quickly check – can you eliminate any choices first? No, there are no answers to eliminate because it looks like all the answers are possibly right because they all add up to 11 rolls.
So just start testing.
4 rolls of quarters (4 x $10) = $40, and 7 rolls of dimes ($7 x $5) = $35, total $75 so that’s not right.
7 rolls of quarters (7 x $10)  = $70, and 4 rolls of dimes ($4 x $5)  = $20, total $90
So, you can stop there as you have found the right answer.

questions.question:
A number line is shown.
What is the distance, in units, from 0 to point
P
on the number line?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b) 4 ½
Explanation:
Be careful with this kind of question. It does not ask what point P is – it asks point P’s distance from 0, which is an absolute value and has no plus or minus.
P is halfway between –5 and –4, so it is 4 ½ units away from 0.
The distance in units is 4 ½.

questions.question:
A restaurant is at 75 percent capacity with 120 patrons.
How many people are in the restaurant when it is at 100 percent capacity?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
a)
160
Explanation:
We will use the proportion method that you learned for solving percentages.
{$\frac{part}{whole} = \frac{percent}{100}$}
If we plug in the values that are given, we can solve the problem. 120/x = 75/100, which simplifies to 120/x = ¾.
Looking at the numerators we can see that 3 x 40 = 120.
So apply the same rule to the denominator to calculate x.
Therefore 4 x 40 = 160.
120/160 = 3/4
120/x = 3/4 can also be rewritten as 120(4)/3 = x  where x = 160.
So the correct answer is 160 patrons in the restaurant at full capacity.

Answer:
d) 9
Explanation:
This is a function question. Apply g(x) = x2 − 1 first to g(3) and then to g(6).
First use a=3 for x: g(3) = {$3^{2}$} − 1 = 8.
So 8 is g(a).
Then use b=6 for x: g(6) = {$6^{2}$} − 1 = 35.
So {${3^{5}$} is g(b) .
Now apply the formula for slope:
{$\frac{g(b)-g(a)}{b-a}$}
Plug in the numbers for a, b, g(a) and g(b).
{$\frac{35-8}{6-3}=\frac{27}{3}=9$}
The rate of change is 9.

questions.question:
Sahil placed a 7–foot ladder against a wall with the base of the ladder 4 feet away from the wall. Then he decided that a longer, 10–foot ladder needed to be used.
If Sahil wants the longer ladder to rest against the wall at the same angle as the shorter ladder, approximately how far away from the wall should he place its base?
(It may help to make a sketch)
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b) 5.7 feet
Explanation:
This is a ratio or proportion question with two triangles.
To keep the ladder at the same angle, the base distance for the 10–foot ladder needs to be in the same proportion to the 10–foot ladder as base distance for the 7–foot ladder is to its 4-foot base.
Set up proportional, equivalent fractions.
Or set up as ratios 4:7 to x:10  solved as 7x = 40.
{$\frac{x}{10}=\frac{4}{7}=\frac{40}{7}\simeq 5.7$}
The ladder needs to be about 5.7 feet from the wall.

questions.question:
This diagram shows a polygon composed of rectangles.
What is the perimeter, in feet, of the polygon?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
d) 210
Explanation:
This question is an addition problem, because the perimeter of a shape = the total length of all the sides. So let’s fill in some measurements that are missing and then add up the sides.(highlighted on the diagram in
RED
)
The long length at the top matches several lengths we have measurements for at the bottom: 22 + 18 + 14 = 54 ft.
The short length at the top matches its opposite side at the bottom so equals 16 ft.
The far right end matches some other vertical lengths we have: 15 + 5 + 5 = 25 ft.
The other missing length at the bottom matches its opposite side and equals 10ft.
Now we have all the lengths so let’s add them up to get the perimeter, starting with the long length at the top and going to the right.
54 + 5 + 16 + 25 + 16 + 5 + 14 + 10 + 18 + 10 + 22 + 15 = 210 feet

questions.question:
Sharon made a scale drawing of a triangular park.  Her scale is 1 unit = 1 meter.
What is the area of the triangular park, in square meters?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) 9 square meters
Explanation:
This question requires you to use coordinates and to use a formula to calculate the area of a triangle. The formula for area of a triangle is A = ½bh, or half the base multiplied by the height.
Let’s calculate the measurements we need to plug into the formula. Looking at the units, which each measure 1 meter, we can see that the base is 6 meters and the height is 3 meters.
A =½(6)(3) or 9 square meters

quizzes.title: Quiz on Video: Apply the Scientific Method

questions.question: What is a hypothesis?
options: The set of 7 steps in the scientific method
questions.explanation:
Answe
r:
a)
An educated guess
Explanation:
A hypothesis is an educated guess and a possible explanation about why something is happening. Forming a hypothesis is one of the steps in the scientific method.

questions.question: How many major steps are there in the scientific method?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c)
7
Explanation:
There are 7 major steps in the scientific method. They are: observation, question, background research, form hypothesis, test with experiment, analyze results, and test results.

questions.question:
What does it mean to
experiment
?
options: To form an educated guess about why something happens
To run a test to find out what happens
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b) To run a test to find out what happens
Explanation:
To experiment means to run a test in order to find out what happens. Scientists run experiments to test whether their hypotheses are true or not.

questions.question:
A farmer notices that the tomato plants in his field grew more tomatoes than the tomato plants under a tree by the barn. He also noticed that the tree protected the plants under it from the rain.
Which part of the scientific method is this?  (Select one)
questions.explanation:
Answer:
d) Observation
Explanation:
The farmer notices something happening to the tomatoes. This represents the scientific method of: Observation

questions.question:
The farmer of the tomato plants wonders, “Do you grow more tomatoes when you give a plant more water?”
Which part of the scientific method is this?  (Select one)
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b) Question
Explanation:
The farmer asks a question about what he sees regarding his tomatoes and the amount of water they need to grow. This represents the scientific method of: Question

questions.question:
The farmer thinks his tomato plants will grow more fruit if they receive more water.
Which part of the scientific method is this?  (Select one)
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) Form Hypothesis
Explanation:
The farmer makes an educated guess to answer his question about his tomatoes. This represents the scientific method of: Form Hypothesis

questions.question:
The farmer grows two rows of tomatoes. The farmer waters one row with 1 liter of water per plant per week. The farmer waters the second row with 2 liters of water per plant per week. The farmer does this for one month.
Which part of the scientific method is this?  (Select one)
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) Test with experiment
Explanation:
The farmer designs an experiment to test his thoughts about his tomatoes. This represents the scientific method of: Test with experiment

questions.question:
After one month of watering, the farmer measures the height of the tomato plants in each row. He compares the two rows. He counts how many tomatoes are growing on each plant, and compares the two rows.
Which part of the scientific method is this?  (Select one)
questions.explanation:
Answer:
d) Analyze results
Explanation:
The farmer compares the rows to analyze the results of his experiment. This represents the scientific method of: Analyze results

questions.question: What do line graphs show?
options: Data in the style of a pie chart
The amount of variables in one month
The amount of change over time
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c)
The amount of change over time
Explanation:
There are many types of graphs. A line graph is used to show the quantity or amount that something changes over time.

questions.question: What is data?
options: Data is the amount of change over time
Data is the average rate of increase on a graph
Data is a style of graph
Data is the information collected in an investigation
questions.explanation:
Answer
:

Explanation:
Data refers to information, such as numbers or amounts. Data is collected by scientists during investigations or experiments.

questions.question: Which of the following methods can you use to track the number of cereal bowls you have for breakfast during a span of 6 months?
options: Use a line graph to record the data
Plot the months along the x-axis
Plot the dependent variable along the y-axis
questions.explanation:

Explanation:
You can use a line graph, with the independent variable data (number of months) along the x-axis and the dependent variable data (number of cereal bowls) along the y-axis.

quizzes.title: Quiz on Video: How To Read a Line Graph

questions.question: What do the x and y axes normally represent in a data graph?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) The data variables
Explanation:
The axes on a graph represent variables. Usually, the independent variable is on the x-axis, and the dependent variable is on the y-axis.

questions.question: Which of the following does the x-axis on a data graph usually represent?
options: Both the dependent and independent variables
Neither the dependent nor the independent variables

a) The independent variable
Explanation:
Usually, the independent variable is on the x-axis.

questions.question: Which of the following does the y-axis on a data graph usually represent?
options: Both the dependent and independent variables
Neither the dependent nor the independent variables

b) The dependent variable
Explanation:
Usually, the dependent variable is on the y-axis.
You can practice finding data in graphs and charts in the quiz at the end of this lesson. There will be more examples to practice on in later lessons. You will be good at reading charts and graphs when you finish the class!

questions.question:

questions.question:
Read the text below. Then answer the questions.
The same text will be used for the next three questions.
Suah’s pet cat has been acting strange lately, and Suah also notices that some of the leaves on her houseplants have been eaten. Suah guesses that something in one of the houseplants is causing the cat to act strangely. She decided to experiment to see which plant was making her cat act strange. On Monday, she hid one plant. On Tuesday, she hid a different plant. She notes how the cat behaves in the absence of each plant. After the cat has had one day away from each plant, Suah has discovered which plant is causing her cat to act strangely.
Question
:
Which of the following is/are the dependent variable(s) in Suah’s experiment?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) The cat’s behavior
Explanation:
The dependent variable is the variable that is being tested or measured and changes with the independent variable.
In this case, the cat’s behavior depended upon both plants.

questions.question:
Suah’s pet cat has been acting strange lately, and Suah also notices that some of the leaves on her houseplants have been eaten. Suah guesses that something in one of the houseplants is causing the cat to act strangely. She decided to experiment to see which plant was making her cat act strange. On Monday, she hid one plant. On Tuesday, she hid a different plant. She notes how the cat behaves in the absence of each plant. After the cat has had one day away from each plant, Suah has discovered which plant is causing her cat to act strangely.
Use the text above to determine your answer.
QUESTION
: Which is/are the independent variable(s) Suah used in her experiment?
options: Both the first and the second plants
questions.explanation:
Answer:
d) Both, the first and the second plants
Explanation:
The independent variable is the variable that may affect or change the dependent variable. In this case,
both the plants
were independent variables that may be affecting the cat’s behavior.

questions.question:
Suah’s pet cat has been acting strange lately, and Suah also notices that some of the leaves on her houseplants have been eaten. Suah guesses that something in one of the houseplants is causing the cat to act strangely. She decided to experiment to see which plant was making her cat act strange. On Monday, she hid one plant. questions.question: Why are statistics useful? (Choose the correct answer)
options: Statistics give us information and show patterns that we may not otherwise notice.
Statistics help scientists find results and present data.
Statistics are helpful for supporting arguments.
questions.explanation:
Answer:

All of the above
Explanation:
Statistics are useful, because they help show patterns in data. This can help support arguments and draw conclusions (or results). Statistics also help scientists present their data findings.

questions.question: According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, the unemployment rate for workers with a high school diploma is 5.4%. The unemployment for workers with less than a high school diploma is 8%. What conclusion can you draw from this statistic?

People who graduate high school have a lower rate of unemployment than those who don't graduate.

People who graduate high school have a lower rate of unemployment than those who don’t graduate.

The data graph shows that the rate of unemployment is lower for workers who have earned a high school diploma (5.4%) than those who do not have a high school diploma (8%).

questions.question: When answering an exam question about statistics in a data table, which of the following is a useful way to analyze the information you’re given?

Look carefully at the question being asked, such as if you're asked to find the average or to calculate something.

All of the above

quizzes.title: Quiz on Video: Mean, Median, and Mode

questions.question: What is another term for the mean in statistics?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
a) The average
Explanation:
The mean is calculated by taking the
sum of all the numbers in a set and then dividing by the total number that was added together. This is also commonly known as finding the average.

questions.question:
What is the
median
in a data set?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b) The middle
Explanation:
The median is the middle value in a data set when arranged from lowest to highest. For example, in the set 2,4,7,9,12 the median is 7.

questions.question:
What is the
mode
in a data set?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
a)
The most
Explanation:
The mode in a data set is the number or value that occurs the most. For example, in the set 2, 2, 5, 8, 9 the mode is 2.

questions.question: What is the mean of the numbers 10, 5, 7, 13, 5?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) 8
Explanation:
The mean is the sum of all the numbers in the set divided by the number of numbers in the set. The sum of the numbers 10 + 5 + 7 + 13 + 5 = 40. Divide 40 by the number of numbers (5):  40/5=8 The mean is 8.

questions.question: What is the mode of the numbers 10, 5, 7, 13, 5?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
a) 5
Explanation:
The mode is the number that occurs most frequently in a set. 5 is listed twice, while the others only once. So 5 is the Mode.

questions.question: What is the median of the numbers 10, 5, 7, 13, 5?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b) 7
Explanation:
The median is the middle number in a set of numbers. From smallest to largest, the numbers are 5, 5, 7, 10, 13.  The median is 7, which is the number in the middle.

questions.question:
Two scientists are designing instant hot and cold packs for a sports company. They want to find a chemical that reacts with water to either heat up or cools down the water inside the packs. They are testing the reaction of ammonium chloride.
They measure the temperature of the water before they add the ammonium chloride. After they add the chemical, they measure the temperature again. To get a good result, they do the test five times. They enter the results in the following table:
What is the average change in water temperature after the reaction takes place?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
a) 22.9 degrees
Explanation:
Have your calculator ready.
First, we calculate the average temperature before the reaction by adding the top line of figures and dividing by 5.
35.4 + 35.5 + 33.2 + 34.7 + 34.4= 173.2 173.2/5 = 34.64.
Then we find the average temperature after the reaction by adding the bottom line of figures and dividing by 5. 11.2 + 12.7 + 10.9 + 11.7 + 12.1 = 58.6
58.6/5 = 11.72, the average temperature after the reaction.
The average temperature went from 34.64 down to 11.72, a change of 22.92 degrees.

questions.question:
Doctors want to find out if protein supplements help their patients recovering from knee surgery. A group of 20 patients recovering from knee surgery is divided into 2 groups of 10 patients each. The 10 patients in Group 1 were given protein supplements. The patients in Group 2 were given no protein supplements.
This table shows how many days each patient in each group took to recover. When the doctors analyzed the data in this table, they found that their patients recovered more quickly on average when they were given protein supplements.
QUESTION
:
Is the doctors’ conclusion true or false?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
a) True
Explanation:
Step 1:
First let’s make sure we understand what the table is telling us. The column on the left lists ten numbers. Are these numbers of patients? The number of supplements? Let’s stop and read the column heading carefully. It says Group 1 (received supplements) number of recovery days. So the numbers in the column are the numbers of days patients took to recover. The same goes for the right–hand column – these are the numbers of recovery days for patients who did not get the supplements.
Step 2:
Now that we understand the data, let’s look at the question. Is it true or false that the patients recovered more quickly on average with supplements? What does “on average” mean? It means we need to figure out the average recovery time of each group to get the answer. We need to calculate the mean.
Step 3:
Now that we understand what we are being asked, let’s do the math! There are 10 patients in each group, so let’s add up Group 1’s recovery days and divide it by 10: 61 total recovery hours divided by 10: 61/10 = 6.1 days average.
Now let’s do Group 2: 70 total recovery hours divided by 10; 70/10 = 7 days average.
Group 1(with supplements) : 6.1 days average
Group 2 (without supplements): 7 days average
It seems based on average recovery time that the answer is true: the supplements did help the patients to recover more quickly, by almost a whole day on average.

quizzes.title: Quiz on Video: Types of Cells

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of prokaryotic cells?

quizzes.title: Quiz on Video: Questions with Scientific Words

questions.question: Which of the following is a good tip to follow when answering exam questions about scientific words?
options: Remember every single detail of the scientific process.
Memorize exactly what each scientific word means before you take the exam.
Use your reading and thinking skills, since these are more important than memorizing exact terms.

You do not need to memorize every scientific term or know every detail of the scientific process. Your reading and thinking skills are more important, since they will help you comprehend (understand) what you need to know in order to choose the correct answers.

questions.question: When answering a question about a passage containing scientific words, what can you do to find the correct answer even if you are not sure of the word meanings?
options: Read each of the answer options carefully and match them with terms in the passage.
Find the meaning of scientific words by interpreting the context of the passage.
Eliminate the wrong choices based on the information in the passage.

All of the above

When answering a question about a passage containing scientific words, it’s helpful to:

and match them with terms in the passage to see if they align.
Interpret the meaning of scientific words through context
, which can give clues to their meaning even if you’re not familiar with the exact term.

based on the information provided, which can help narrow down the correct answer even if you’re unsure.

questions.question: What skill does the Science portion of the GED Exam test?
options: Your comprehension (understanding) of readings and examples
Your ability to use your thinking and reasoning skills
Your ability to understand context and passages.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
d)
All of the above
Explanation:
The Science portion of the GED exam tests your ability to:
Comprehend readings and examples
(understanding scientific texts and data),
Use your thinking and reasoning skills
(applying critical thinking to solve problems),
Understand context and passages
(interpreting information in scientific scenarios).
These skills are key to performing well on the exam, as it focuses on reasoning through scientific concepts rather than just memorizing facts.

quizzes.title: Quiz on Video: Cell Division Processes

questions.question: What types of cells does mitosis produce?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b)
Diploid cells
Explanation:
Mitosis produces
diploid cells
, meaning the daughter cells have the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell (in humans, this is 46 chromosomes). The daughter cells are genetically identical to the parent cell and to each other.
Haploid cells, which have half the number of chromosomes, are produced through meiosis, not mitosis.

questions.question: What types of cells does meiosis produce?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
a) Haploid cells
Explanation:
Meiosis produces
haploid cells
, which contain half the number of chromosomes compared to the original cell. In humans, this means the resulting cells have 23 chromosomes. These cells are gametes (sperm and egg cells), used in sexual reproduction.
Meiosis does not produce cells for growth and repair (those are produced through mitosis), and the cells produced by meiosis are
not genetically identical
—they have genetic variation due to the process of crossing over and independent assortment.

questions.question: What do mitosis and meiosis both do?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) Create cell division
Explanation:
Both mitosis and meiosis involve
cell division
:
Mitosis
is the process that results in the division of a single cell into two identical diploid cells for growth, repair, and asexual reproduction.
Meiosis
is a specialized type of cell division that produces haploid gametes (sperm and egg cells) for sexual reproduction.
Mitosis is responsible for growth and repair, but meiosis is not. Neither process involves cell fusion; that occurs during fertilization in sexual reproduction.

questions.question:
Read this passage of text and answer the question. Use your test tip for understanding questions about scientific text.
(Remember to read the question carefully)
Although cells vary in size, they’re generally quite small. For instance, the diameter of a typical human red blood cell is about eight micrometers (0.008 millimeters). To give you some context, the head of a pin is about one millimeter in diameter, so about 125 red blood cells could be lined up in a row across the head of a pin. With a few exceptions, individual cells cannot be seen with the naked eye, so scientists must instead use microscopes (micro– = “small”; –scope = “to look at”) to study them. A microscope is an instrument that magnifies objects otherwise too small to be seen, producing an image in which the object appears larger. Most photographs of cells are taken using a microscope, and these pictures can also be called micrographs.
From the definition above, it might sound like a microscope is just a kind of magnifying glass. In fact, magnifying glasses do qualify as microscopes; since they have just one lens, they are called simple microscopes. The fancier instruments that we typically think of as microscopes are compound microscopes, meaning that they have multiple lenses. Because of the way these lenses are arranged, they can bend light to produce a much more magnified image than that of a magnifying glass.”
QUESTION
: Based on the information in the test, what meaning does the word microscope contain? Choose the best answer.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b) Looking at small things
Explanation:
The text says the word microscope combines two meanings: “micro,” which means small, and “scope,” which means to look at. The answer that contains both these meanings is
b
: “Looking at small things.”

questions.question:
Read this passage of text and answer the question.
(Remember to read the question carefully)
It may seem obvious now that we, and other living things, are made up of cells. Prior to the 1600s, however, it wasn’t obvious at all, for the simple reason that no one had ever seen a cell up close and personal. To distinguish individual cells in a piece of tissue or individual bacteria in a sample of liquid required the development of relatively high–powered microscopes, instruments used for magnifying objects otherwise too small to be seen. For more on how microscopes are used in biology today, check out the article on microscopy.
The first person to observe cells as microscopic structures was the British scientist Robert Hooke. In fact, he was the person who gave cells their name. In his book Micrographia, he used the term cell to refer to the box–like structures he saw when he looked at dead cork tissue through a simple microscope. He chose the cell as the name because these boxes reminded him of the cells of a monastery, the simple rooms in which monks slept.
The cells that Hooke observed, however, were in dead tissue, and were in fact cell walls left behind after the death of the real cells. The first person to observe living, moving cells was Anton van Leeuwenhoek, a Dutch shopkeeper and crafter of lenses. In the 1670s, inspired by Hooke’s book, he began to build his own, more powerful microscopes. With these, he was able to observe living single–celled organisms—such as bacteria—and sperm cells, which he collectively called animalcules.
QUESTION
: Which sentence below best describes the main idea in this passage of text? Choose the best answer.
options: All living things are made of cells.

“Mitochondria are small organelles present in most of the body’s cells which function in the conversion of certain chemicals in our food, in the presence of oxygen, to the common currency of energy inside cells (ATP). Mitochondria contain their own private DNA. In recent years, more than 20 hereditary disorders have been shown to result from mutations in mitochondrial DNA. Because mitochondria come only from the egg, most mitochondria–related disorders are inherited exclusively from the mother. Mitochondrial disorders can appear at any age in males or females, with a wide variety of non–specific symptoms and signs. These disorders may cause metabolic disturbances, developmental delay, blindness, hearing loss, heart rhythm problems, short stature, and gastrointestinal problems.”

questions.question:

Mitosis is a type of cell division in which the two daughter cells that are formed have the same genetic material as the parent cell. Before mitosis starts each chromosome in the nucleus duplicates itself to produce two sections called chromatids which are linked. Those chromatids then split so that each daughter cell has DNA identical to that of the parent cell and to that of the other daughter cell. The function of the spindle fiber in mitosis is to control the movement of chromatids during mitosis during the metaphase. The spindle fiber helps to align the chromatids and a line across the middle of the cell so that the chromatids can divide evenly during anaphase. The spindle fibers then direct the movement of chromatids after they split ensuring that each daughter cell has a full set of identical chromatids.

questions.question:
Read this passage of text. Then answer the question using your test tip about testing statements against the data.
Multicellular organisms
Most cells in large multicellular organisms don’t directly exchange substances like nutrients and wastes with the external environment. Instead, they are surrounded by an internal environment of extracellular fluid—literally, fluid outside of cells. The cells get oxygen and nutrients from this extracellular fluid and release waste products into it. Humans and other complex organisms have specialized systems that maintain the internal environment, keeping it steady and able to provide for the needs of the cells.
QUESTION
: Based on this passage of text, is the following statement true or false?
The majority of cells in a large living thing are in direct contact with the outside environment.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
False
Explanation:
The correct answer is false because the test tells us that most cells in large multicellular organisms don’t directly exchange substances … with the external environment. Organisms are living things. External means outside. The text also tells us that most cells in large organisms are surrounded by an internal environment … So they are not in direct contact with the outside world.

questions.question:
Read this passage of text from your last quiz. Then answer the question using your test tip about testing statements against the data.
Microscopes and lenses
Although cells vary in size, they’re generally quite small. For instance, the diameter of a typical human red blood cell is about eight micrometers (0.008 millimeters). To give you some context, the head of a pin is about one millimeter in diameter, so about 125 red blood cells could be lined up in a row across the head of a pin. With a few exceptions, individual cells cannot be seen with the naked eye, so scientists must instead use microscopes (micro– = “small”; –scope = “to look at”) to study them. A microscope is an instrument that magnifies objects otherwise too small to be seen, producing an image in which the object appears larger. Most photographs of cells are taken using a microscope, and these pictures can also be called micrographs.
From the definition above, it might sound like a microscope is just a kind of magnifying glass. In fact, magnifying glasses do qualify as microscopes; since they have just one lens, they are called simple microscopes. The fancier instruments that we typically think of as microscopes are compound microscopes, meaning that they have multiple lenses. Because of the way these lenses are arranged, they can bend light to produce a much more magnified image than that of a magnifying glass.
Based on the information in the text, which of these statements is true?
Choose the best answer.
options: Magnifying glasses are a type of microscope.
Micrographs are a type of microscope.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
a) Magnifying glasses are a type of microscope
Explanation:
The passage states that magnifying glasses qualify as microscopes and are classified as simple microscopes because they have just one lens.
The other statements are incorrect:
b)
is false because microscopes can have a single lens (like magnifying glasses).
c)
is false because micrographs are images taken with microscopes, not types of microscopes.
d)
is false because the passage does not state that microscopes must show cells; they magnify objects that are too small to be seen, which could include other small items as well.

questions.question:
Read this passage of text and answer the question.
“Discovering cells
:
It may seem obvious now that we, and other living things, are made up of cells. Prior to the 1600s, however, it wasn’t obvious at all, for the simple reason that no one had ever seen a cell up close and personal. To distinguish individual cells in a piece of tissue or individual bacteria in a sample of liquid required the development of relatively high–powered microscopes, instruments used for magnifying objects otherwise too small to be seen. For more on how microscopes are used in biology today, check out the article on microscopy.
The first person to observe cells as microscopic structures was the British scientist Robert Hooke. In fact, he was the person who gave cells their name. In his book Micrographia, he used the term cell to refer to the box–like structures he saw when he looked at dead cork tissue through a simple microscope. He chose the cell as the name because these boxes reminded him of the cells of a monastery, the simple rooms in which monks slept.
The cells that Hooke observed, however, were in dead tissue, and were in fact cell walls left behind after the death of the real cells. The first person to observe living, moving cells was Anton van Leeuwenhoek, a Dutch shopkeeper and crafter of lenses. In the 1670s, inspired by Hooke’s book, he began to build his own, more powerful microscopes. With these, he was able to observe living single–celled organisms—such as bacteria—and sperm cells, which he collectively called animalcules.”
Why did Anton van Leeuwenhoek begin to build more powerful microscopes?
options: Because he wanted to see cells move.
Because he wanted to collect animalcules.
Because he had read “Micrographia” by Robert Hooke.
Because he wanted to sell microscopes in his shop.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c)
Because he had read “Micrographia” by Robert Hooke
Explanation:
By testing the statements against the test, we can quickly see which one is true. The text tells us that in the 1670s, Anton van Leeuwenhoek was “inspired by Hooke’s book” and “he began to build his own, more powerful microscopes.”

questions.question: Brown eyes (B) are genetically dominant over blue eyes (b). If Amelia has a brown-eye gene and a blue-eye gene (Bb), what color eyes does Amelia have?

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the Punnett square diagram?
options: It is best for predicting complex genetic inheritance with great accuracy.
It is highly precise for predicting random variations and outcomes observed in small samples and individual families.
It is highly effective in estimating exact distribution of genotypes and phenotypes when there is a linkage between two genes.
It is a useful model for understanding the basics of how meiosis and fertilization result in various possible genotypes and phenotypes of offspring.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
d)
It is a useful model for understanding the basics of how meiosis and fertilization result in various possible genotypes and phenotypes of offspring.
Explanation:
a)
This is not true because the Punnett square is not best suited for complex traits, which often involve multiple genes and interactions.
b)
The Punnett square provides probabilities rather than precise predictions, especially in small sample sizes.
c)
While it can illustrate potential combinations of alleles, it does not provide exact distributions when genes are linked, as real-world outcomes can be affected by additional factors.
d)
This accurately reflects the purpose of a Punnett square, which helps visualize and predict the genetic combinations that can arise from the alleles of the parents during meiosis and fertilization.

questions.question:
A green-eyed mother and a brown-eyed father are expecting a child. Brown (B) is a dominant gene and green (b) is a recessive gene.
What are the chances that the child will have the same eye color as the mother?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) 50%
Explanation and Answer:
The eye color inheritance pattern can be understood using a Punnett square. The green-eyed mother has the genotype **bb**, and the brown-eyed father has the genotype **Bb** (heterozygous).
We set up a Punnett square with the mother’s alleles on one side and the father’s alleles on the other:
From this, we get the following possible genotypes for the child:
– Bb (brown eyes) — 50% chance
– bb (green eyes) — 50% chance
Since the mother has green eyes, and green eyes correspond to the
bb
genotype, there is a 50% chance that the child will inherit the bb genotype and have green eyes like the mother.
Thus, the correct answer is:
c) 50%**

questions.question:
An apple tree with red apples (Aa) has a dominant red–apple gene (A) and a recessive yellow–apple gene (a). It is crossed with another apple tree with the same traits (Aa).
QUESTION
: What is the chance that the trees’
offspring will have yellow apples?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) 25%
Explanation:
The quickest way to figure out the answer is to put the information into a Punnett square.
Then the answer is clear. If two trees with Aa cross, you can see that A is dominant in three out of the four squares. The offspring has a three out four chance of being a red–apple tree. So that leaves only one chance out of four for a yellow–apple tree (aa).
One out of four is the same as 25%.

questions.question: Add the appropriate number in the blank below
questions.explanation:
Answer:
2
Explanation:

Dominants need 1 or 2, however, recessive must have 2.

questions.question:
GED, HiSET, and TASC tests often have more than one question about the same data. The questions make you look at the data in different ways to get different information. So here is a different question about the data you already saw in your test tip.
A population of a certain species of mammal was studied over many generations. The graph above shows the percentages of fur colors observed in the population over the generations.
Which explanation is the most likely reason for the appearance of individuals that have white fur?
options: The mammals chose a different food source that resulted in a new fur color.
The mammals adapted to a change in climate by changing their fur color.
A mutation occurred in an individual’s fur color gene and resulted in a new fur color.
A new predator moved into the area that caused the individuals to change fur color.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c)A mutation occurred in an individual’s fur color gene and resulted in a new fur color.
Explanation:
Mutations can cause changes in genes. The changes are passed down. The most likely answer, looking at the graph, is that a mutated gene created a new color (white) and that the new color got passed down to more and more bears as time went by. If the bears lived in a snowy region, white would be good for camouflage against the snow. The climate would not cause the change, but the mutation would be a good change, making the bear more fit than brown bears or black bears in the same region.
If a mutation makes an organism more fit, then natural selection will take place, and the mutation will stay in the species.

questions.question:
In 1991, the Environment Agency of Japan did a survey to identify native Japanese species of animals that were in danger of extinction. The agency published its figures in a table called Japanese Wildlife in Danger of Extinction.
Use the information in the table above to answer the question.
Extinct, endangered, vulnerable and rare mammals in Japan are all in danger of disappearing. What fraction of them were actually extinct in 1991?
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) 1/11th
Explanation:
To find the fraction of mammals that were extinct in 1991, we first need to calculate the total number of mammals that were in danger of disappearing. This includes those listed as extinct, endangered, vulnerable, or rare.
From the table:
Extinct mammals: 5
Endangered mammals: 3
Vulnerable mammals: 11
Rare mammals: 36
Now, add these categories to get the total number of mammals in danger of disappearing:
5+3+11+36=55
The fraction of mammals that were actually extinct is:
{$\frac{5}{55}=\frac{1}{11}$}
So, the fraction of mammals that were extinct in 1991 is {$\frac{1}{11}$}

questions.question:

questions.explanation:
Answer:
d) 34,314 will be left
Explanation:
You needed your calculator to make three quick calculations to find this answer:
1. Add together the vertebrate and invertebrate subtotals for all native species in column 1: 1,199 + 33,776 = 34,975)
2. Add together the vertebrate and invertebrate subtotals for all native species in danger in column 6 (258 + 403 = 661)
3. Subtract the species in danger from the total species (34,975 – 661 = 34,314)
So, the answer is 34,314.
When there are answers that do not correspond to the question, you can quickly eliminate (get rid of) those. They are just there so you pay careful attention to what the question is asking!

questions.question:
Read the text below and then answer the question:
“A few years ago, scientists found oceans are ten times more noisy in the 2000s than they were in the 1960s. The noise comes from the vast increase in the global shipping trade, the number of ships on the world’s oceans, and the higher speeds and power of individual ships.
The following paragraph is from a New York Times story about an ecological study. Please read the paragraph and then answer the question below.
“Mud crabs don’t have ears, but they can still detect and react to noises. When exposed to sounds made by preying fish, the crabs were less likely to feed on their own meals, researchers at Northeastern University reported last week. Listening for danger is a critical part of the crab’s survival strategy that could be hindered by increasing ocean noise, the scientists concluded.”
Question: Is the following statement true or false?

Excerpt from newsela.com adaptation of the Christian Science Monitor, December 1, 2017,
“Predicting earthquakes
Recently, a team of scientists suggested that 2018 and the following four years could bring more strong earthquakes than usual.
As Earth’s rotation speeds up, the equator expands slightly. As Earth slows, the equator shrinks. Scientists Professor Bendick and Dr. Bilham think the added stress of that change might add an extra nudge of pressure on tectonic plates. It pushes faults that are already on the verge of an earthquake over the edge.
Studying history, the scientists noticed that there tended to be more tremors during Earth’s slowest rotation rate. The planet is currently in such a slowdown. So, the scientists now predict there will be more large earthquakes. According to their calculations, the likelihood of magnitude 7 or greater earthquakes is roughly 25 percent to 30 percent higher during the next five years, particularly around the equator. If this hypothesis proves to be true, it could be another key tool for forecasters. It could help earthquake-prone regions near the equator to better prepare for a quake.”

It could help earthquake-prone regions near the equator to better prepare for a quake.
questions.explanation:

The scientists noticed that there tended to be more tremors during Earth’s slowest rotation rate.
Explanation:

questions.question:
Read the text and choose the best answer to the question below.
Excerpt adapted from the Washington Post, March 6, 2017,
How old is Earth?
Shortly after radioactivity was discovered in 1896, scientists realized they could figure out how old rock was by measuring how much of the uranium in it had decayed into lead. This process is called radiometric dating.
When a rock is formed in the bowels of the planet, uranium atoms are trapped within it. These atoms will decay as the rock ages. Radiometric dating measures the ratio of radioactive isotopes within the rock. From this, scientists can figure out how long it has been around.
In 1913, geologist Arthur Holmes published “The Age of the Earth,” the first major effort to date the planet using radiometric dating.
He estimated that Earth was about 1.6 billion years old. Holmes later revised his number. By the 1940s, the geology community had mostly accepted his revised estimate of about 4.5 billion years — a number not far from the one we use today.
QUESTION: What evidence did Arthur Holmes give to support his theory about the age of Earth?
options: Measurements of the number of uranium atoms
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b) Measurements of radioactive isotopes
Explanation:
The evidence Arthur Holmes gave to support his theory about the age of Earth is:
Measurements of radioactive isotopes
Holmes used radiometric dating, which involves measuring the ratio of radioactive isotopes, like uranium decaying into lead, to estimate the age of rocks and, by extension, the Earth. This method allowed him to estimate the Earth’s age at around 1.6 billion years, later revised to 4.5 billion years.

Adapted from ProCon.org
Viewpoint 1
According to a Dec. 2013 study in Nature Geoscience, the Sun has had only a “minor effect” on the climate over the past 1,000 years. Another 2013 study found that solar activity could not have contributed to more than 10% of the observed global warming over the 20th century.

questions.question:
Read the views about climate change below. Then answer the question.
Adapted from ProCon.org
Opinion 1
We are statistically more confident that humans cause climate change than that smoking causes cancer. The research falls into several lines of evidence, including
1. Simple chemistry that when we burn carbon-based materials, carbon dioxide (CO2) is emitted
2. Records of how much CO2 human activities emit
3. Measuring CO2 in the atmosphere shows that levels are higher than anything we’ve seen in hundreds of thousands of years
4. Chemical analysis of the atmospheric CO2 that reveals the increase is coming from burning fossil fuels

Climate has been changing since the Earth was formed, some 4.5 billion years ago. Climate changes on every time scale – whether decades, centuries, or millennia.
Many sincere people, without the time or training to dig into the facts, have been misled by the demonization of carbon dioxide. This seems to be a recurrent feature of human history. Opinion 1 provides several lines of evidence, including chemical principles, empirical data on CO2 emissions, historical atmospheric records, and correlations between CO2 levels and climate warming.
