questions.question:
Read the following text about the Greek scientist Eratosthenes. Then answer the question
Eratosthenes
Early scientists believed their world was probably a sphere, the shape of a ball. But they did not know the size of Earth until about 240 BCE when Eratosthenes performed a scientific experiment.
Eratosthenes received a letter from a friend in Syene, a city in southern Egypt. In the letter, his friend mentioned that at the time of the summer solstice, the Sun would be directly overhead, and nothing would have a shadow. That is, if you had a completely vertical (straight up and down) object, it would not have a shadow.
But Eratosthenes knew that this wasn’t the case in northern Egypt. At exactly the same time on that same day, vertical objects do have shadows. The Sun’s rays were coming from the same direction as the rays shining on Syene. But the rays were hitting Earth at a different angle.
Eratosthenes was a scientist, so he did an experiment. He measured the length of the shadow cast by a vertical stick at noon on the day of the summer solstice. From the length, he figured out the angle of the Sun in relation to the vertical stick placed at Alexandria, the city he lived in. The angle measured one-fiftieth of a circle or 7.2 degrees.
Eratosthenes also measured the distance between the two cities. With the angle and the distance, Eratosthenes was able to calculate the curve in Earth’s surface. He used that to figure out the circumference (the distance around). His calculations were amazingly accurate, even using such simple scientific methods.
QUESTION: What observation led Eratosthenes to perform his experiment?
options: The Sun is in different places at noon on the day of the summer solstice.
A completely vertical object casts no shadow in northern Egypt.
Syene was in northern Egypt and Alexandria was in southern Egypt.
The angle of the Sun’s rays is different at noon in different places.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
d) The angle of the Sun’s rays is different at noon in different places.
Explanation:
This observation led Eratosthenes to perform his experiment, as he recognized that while the Sun was directly overhead in Syene, the rays were hitting Alexandria at a different angle, causing vertical objects to cast shadows.

questions.question:
Read the following text about the Greek scientist Eratosthenes. Then answer the question
Eratosthenes
Early scientists believed their world was probably a sphere, the shape of a ball. But they did not know the size of Earth until about 240 BCE when Eratosthenes performed a scientific experiment.
Eratosthenes received a letter from a friend in Syene, a city in southern Egypt. In the letter, his friend mentioned that at the time of the summer solstice, the Sun would be directly overhead, and nothing would have a shadow. That is, if you had a completely vertical (straight up and down) object, it would not have a shadow.
But Eratosthenes knew that this wasn’t the case in northern Egypt. At exactly the same time on that same day, vertical objects do have shadows. The Sun’s rays were coming from the same direction as the rays shining on Syene. But the rays were hitting Earth at a different angle.
Eratosthenes was a scientist, so he did an experiment. He measured the length of the shadow cast by a vertical stick at noon on the day of the summer solstice. From the length, he figured out the angle of the Sun in relation to the vertical stick placed at Alexandria, the city he lived in. The angle measured one-fiftieth of a circle or 7.2 degrees.
Eratosthenes also measured the distance between the two cities. With the angle and the distance, Eratosthenes was able to calculate the curve in Earth’s surface. He used that to figure out the circumference (the distance around). His calculations were amazingly accurate, even using such simple scientific methods.
QUESTION: What did Eratosthenes calculate that enabled him to figure out Earth’s circumference?
options: The angle of two sticks in two different places
questions.explanation:
Answer:

Explanation:
Eratosthenes measured the angle of the Sun in relation to vertical sticks in Syene and Alexandria. This angle, along with the distance between the two cities, allowed him to calculate the curve of Earth’s surface and ultimately determine its circumference.

a)
the angle of the two sticks in two different places, which provided him with the necessary information to calculate the circumference based on the known distance between the cities.
So, while both
a
and
c
are interconnected, the best answer to the specific question about what Eratosthenes calculated to figure out Earth’s circumference is

the angle of two sticks in two different places.

questions.question:
Before 1781, the only planets that were known were the ones visible to the naked eye, Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. In 1781, William Herschel, an astronomer who made his own superb and powerful telescopes, discovered a strange ‘star’ that appeared as a greenish disc rather than the point of light. A few nights later, he observed that the star had moved relative to the background of the other stars. Herschel realized that he discovered another planet. It was named Uranus after the Greek Sky God. Later it was found that Uranus had actually been observed at least 20 times before, as far back as 1690, but each time it had been identified as a star.
QUESTION: Which of the following is an unstated assumption that could help account for the fact that Uranus was misidentified as a star prior to 1781.

Uranus was not clearly visible in the telescope channel in use at that time

According to the information given, Herschel made excellent powerful telescopes. He probably saw a much sharper image of Uranus than the previous astronomers and was, therefore, able to recognize this unique color and shape.

questions.explanation:
Answer:
b) -2
Explanation:
The charge of an atom is calculated based on the difference between the number of protons and electrons it contains.
Here’s how you can determine the charge:
Identify the Number of Protons
: This is equal to the atomic number of the element and is always a positive charge (+1 for each proton).
Identify the Number of Electrons
: In a neutral atom, the number of electrons is equal to the number of protons, resulting in no overall charge. However, if the atom gains or loses electrons, it becomes an ion.
Calculate the Charge
:
The charge can be calculated using the formula:
{$\text{Charge} = \text{Number of Protons} – \text{Number of Electrons}$}.
In this case,
Charge= 2-4 = -2
If the atom has more protons than electrons, it has a
positive charge
.
If the atom has more electrons than protons, it has a
negative charge
.

The platform is 2.5 meters high. You need to take a 20–kilogram box to the top. But you are not strong enough to lift it that high.

questions.explanation:
Answer: c) 12.5meters
Explanation:
The (background) information tells you that the mechanical advantage of a ramp is the length of the plane divided by the height. The height is 2.5 meters. The mechanical advantage is 5. What do you need to find?
To solve this, you need to find the length of the ramp required to achieve a mechanical advantage of 5.
The mechanical advantage (MA) of a ramp is given by the formula:
{$MA=\frac{length of the ramp}{height of the ramp}$}
In this case:
The mechanical advantage (MA) is 5.
The height of the ramp is 2.5 meters.
Rearranging the formula to solve for the length of the ramp:
Length of the ramp=MA×Height of the ramp
L = 2.5 x 5 = 12.5
So, you need a ramp that is 12.5 meters long.

questions.question:
Read the text. Then, answer the question.
Putting Out Fires
Fire, or combustion, is a useful chemical reaction. However, sometimes, a fire gets out of control and must be put out. There are several ways to do this. All methods of putting out fire work by removing something the reaction needs in order to continue.
One way of putting out a fire is to take away one of the substances that is used in the reaction. The simplest way to do this is to remove the fuel or the material that is burning. You do this when you turn off the gas on the stove.
In a raging fire, it is hard to remove the fuel. It is easier to remove the oxygen that is needed to keep the reaction going. A small fire can be smothered. Baking soda can be poured on a small grease fire on a stovetop. The layer of baking soda keeps oxygen away from the grease, which is the fuel. Smothering a campfire with dirt works the same way.

options: All offspring will be yellow because yellow is dominant.
The ratio of yellow offspring to green offspring will be 1 to 1 or 50%. Offspring have an equal chance of being yellow or green.
The ratio of green offspring to yellow offspring will be 1 to 4.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) The ratio of yellow offspring will be 1 to 1 or 50%. Offspring have an equal chance of being yellow or green
Explanation:
The Punnett square illustrating the combinations shows that two of the possible gene combinations result in offspring inheriting a yellow gene and being yellow, because yellow is dominant over green. Two do not get a yellow gene, so they will be green. Therefore, the offspring has an equal chance of being yellow or green.

questions.question:
Read the text and then answer the question.
Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere
Carbon dioxide is a gas present in small amounts in Earth’s atmosphere. Carbon dioxide is absorbed and released as part of natural cycles that involve ecosystems, the ocean, the atmosphere, and other systems on Earth. The amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere affects Earth’s global temperature and climate.
The amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere is also affected by certain human activities. For example, when fossil fuels are burned, they release carbon dioxide. Fossil fuels include coal, oil, and natural gas. Fossil fuels are used primarily as energy sources for transportation and for producing electricity. Oil is refined into gasoline and other fuels burned by cars, trucks, buses, and airplanes. Most power plants burn coal or natural gas to produce electricity for cities and towns.
Many scientists are concerned because the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere has been increasing over the last century. During this same time period, Earth’s global temperature has also increased. These scientists are concerned that a continued increase in carbon dioxide may cause further changes in Earth’s climate.
QUESTION: Which of these solutions would best help reduce the amount of carbon dioxide released into the atmosphere by human activities?
options: Using rechargeable batteries in small electrical devices
Using more alternative energy sources, such as solar and wind, to produce electricity
Finding more sources of fossil fuels to extract through drilling and mining
Manufacturing more vehicles, such as cars and trucks, for use in transportation
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b) Using more alternative energy sources, such as solar and wind, to produce electricity
Explanation:
The text gave you a clue when it told you the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere is affected by human activities and continues to diss the need for resources to produce energy that are not a type of fossil fuels, which burn and have a negative impact on Earth’s climate. Using alternative energy sources, instead of fossil fuels, to produce electricity would significantly reduce the amount of carbon dioxide released.

questions.question:
Use the following information to answer the question.
The diagram shows a cross–section of an area where two tectonic plates of Earth’s surface are moving towards each other. The leading edge of one tectonic plate has oceanic crust, while the leading edge of the other tectonic plate has continental crust.
QUESTION: Which of these factors could explain the motion of the tectonic plates shown in the diagram?
options: Gravitational pull of the Sun and Moon on Earth’s surface
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) Slow-moving magma within Earth’s interior
The diagram shows two huge pieces of Earth’s surface, called
tectonic plates
, crashing into each other. Specifically, the heavy
Oceanic Crust
is sinking under the lighter
Continental Crust
.
This movement is not caused by things on the surface, like ocean currents or the pull of the Moon. Instead, it’s caused by intense heat and motion deep
inside the Earth
in a layer called the
mantle
.
What’s Happening:
The mantle contains extremely hot, semi-liquid rock (we often call it
magma
or molten rock).
The Driver:
This hot rock moves in giant, slow circles called
convection currents
. Think of it like boiling soup: the hot material rises, moves across the top, cools and sinks, then heats up again.
The Effect:
These slow, powerful currents drag the massive tectonic plates along the Earth’s surface, causing them to spread apart, slide past each other, or crash together as shown in the diagram.
Therefore, the
slow-moving magma within Earth’s interior
is the force that makes these plates move.

The American robin
The American robin is a common songbird found throughout North America. It feeds mostly on insects, fruits, and berries. Its average lifespan is abut 2 years. Only 25 percent of robins survive after one year. Despite this seemingly low survival rate, the American robin is among the most abundant species in North America. To help maintain stability, there are a number of interrelated nonliving (abiotic) factors and living (biotic) factors that act as checks and balances on the growth of a population.
QUESTION: Which four factors are biotic factors that could affect a robin population? Choose ALL the biotic factors.
options: Competition for food and nesting sites
questions.explanation:
Answers:
Reproductive rate
Resistance to disease and parasites,
Ability to hide from predators
Competition for food and nesting sites.
Explanation:
The text gave you a clue when it told you that biotic means living. Pollution and weather conditions are nonliving factors. The other four answers apply to the living robins. So those are the four answers to check.

questions.question:
Read the text. Then choose the best answer to the question.
The effect of acidity on the hearing of fish
Dissolved carbon dioxide gas ({$CO_{2}$} ) creates carbonic acid in ocean water. Rising ocean acidity levels may harm marine life. For example, high acid levels may cause hearing loss. Scientists conducted an investigation to study the effect of increased acidity on fish hearing.
A group of fertilized fish eggs from the same parents were divided into four different aquariums, each with a different pressure of {$CO_{2}$} . One tank contained the normal atmospheric conditions of 390 micro atmospheres of {$CO_{2}$} . The other tanks contained 600, 700, and 900 micro atmospheres of {$CO_{2}$} , respectively. The same number of eggs was placed into each aquarium. The eggs hatched and the fish lived in these aquariums until testing.
To prepare for the experiment, one fish was placed into an aquarium containing the same {$CO_{2}$} pressure in which it was raised. The fish’s position was recorded every 5 seconds for 2 minutes. Then sounds from a predatory fish were played from an underwater speaker at one end of the aquarium at a volume that was only audible to the fish when swimming near the speaker. The fish’s position was again recorded every 5 seconds for 2 minutes. Trials were repeated with fish from each tank.
The study showed that fish raised in elevated {$CO_{2}$} levels did not avoid the sounds of the predator fish. They spent approximately the same proportion of time at the speaker end of the aquarium before and after the sounds of the predator fish were played. However, the fish from the aquarium with the normal atmospheric {$CO_{2}$} pressure avoided the speaker end of the aquarium after the predator sounds were played.
QUESTION: What are the independent and dependent variables in the investigation?
options: Independent = {$CO_{2}$} pressure, Dependent = Position of fish
Independent = Number of eggs in aquarium, Dependent = {$CO_{2}$}  pressure
Independent = Temperature of the water, Dependent = {$CO_{2}$}  pressure
Independent = Position of fish, Dependent = Number of eggs in aquarium
questions.explanation:
Answer:
a)
Independent ={$CO_{2}$}
pressure,
Dependent
= Position of fish
Explanation:
a) Independent = pressure, Dependent = Position of fish.
This is because:
The
independent variable
is the one that is changed (in this case, the
pressure of carbon dioxide
), and it directly affects the
dependent variable
, which is what is being measured (in this case, the
position of the fish
).
The other options do not accurately reflect the variables as described in the experiment:
b)
incorrectly suggests that the number of eggs was a variable, but it was constant across the tanks.
c)
introduces temperature, which was not a variable in this experiment.
d)
incorrectly suggests that the position of fish was an independent variable, which is not the case.
So, to summarize: the only correct answer is
a

All of these items are considered primary sources, because they were created by people during the time being studied, in this case, the American Revolution.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a secondary source about the American Civil War?

a college professor giving a modern day lecture about the Civil War

A college professor giving a modern day lecture can be very informative. But, the professor was not alive during the time of the Civil War. Therefore, this is considered a secondary source.

questions.question: What makes primary sources different from secondary sources?
options: Primary sources are true, and secondary sources are false
Primary sources are evidence, and secondary sources are opinion
Primary sources present one side of the story, and secondary sources present an opposing view
questions.explanation:

Both primary and secondary sources can be very useful. But, primary sources are considered evidence, while secondary sources are considered opinions.

questions.question: What is the primary source?
options: A source found in an important book, like an encyclopedia
A source created at the time of an event by an individual who was there
A source created after an event has happened
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) A source created at the time of an event by an individual who was there.
Explanation:
A primary source is a source that was created by people who were there during the time being studied. It does not need to be a source used often. Sources created after the event happened and sources found in encyclopedias are secondary sources.

questions.question: What is a secondary source?
options: A source which is someone's second choice to use for research.
A source created after an event has happened by someone not present at the event.
A second piece of information written about an event.
A source created at the time of an event.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b) A source created after an event has happened by someone not present at the event.
Explanation:
A secondary source is any source created after the event happened by someone who was not there at the time. Secondary sources can be great sources, like encyclopedia articles or lectures by experts on the subject.

questions.question:
Read this short essay
The Boston Massacre
(adapted from ducksters.com)
The Boston Massacre occurred on March 5, 1770. The colonists were already angry about British soldiers who had been brought to Boston to keep the colonists in order. Colonists had gathered outside Boston’s Custom House. An object thrown from the crowd struck one of the soldiers, and the soldiers fired into the crowd.
Crispus Attucks, an African American Patriot, was the first man killed at the Boston Massacre. His death is often considered the first casualty of the American Revolution. In all, five colonists died – three immediately and two more later from wounds.
The Boston Massacre became a rallying cry for patriotism in the colonies. Groups such as the Sons of Liberty used it to show how bad British rule was. Although the American Revolution would not start for another five years, the event certainly moved people to look at British rule in a different light.
Question
: What is the main point of this text?
options: The Sons of Liberty fought against British rule.
Crispus Attucks was the first casualty of the American Revolution.
The Boston Massacre was a significant event leading to the American Revolution.
British soldiers came to Boston to kill the Patriots.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) The Boston Massacre was a significant event leading to the American Revolution.
Explanation:
The main point or main idea of this text is that the Boston Massacre was a significant event that led to the American Revolution. One line of the text that supports this idea is “The Boston Massacre became a rallying cry for patriotism in the colonies.”

questions.question:
Read the following passage. Then answers the question.
In 1775, the 13 colonies met and debated over whether they should declare their independence from Britain. The decision was difficult, for there was no guarantee they would win the war. Each colony sent representatives to the Second Continental Congress to decide how and when to officially cut ties with the British Empire. By the summer of 1776, they had made their decision.
They settled on the Declaration of Independence, written by Thomas Jefferson. This document declared that the colonies would unite as states to become their own country. It also listed the reasons for their separation, including the abuses of power they had endured for so long. Twelve out of the 13 colonies voted in favor of independence on July 2, 1776. The Second Continental Congress officially adopted the document on July 4, 1776, and the United States became independent.
(Courtesy of commonlit.org)
Question: What is this passage about?
Choose the best answer.
options: How Thomas Jefferson was chosen to write the Declaration of Independence
How the colonists came together to make a decision to declare independence
How difficult it was to win the war against the British
How colonists were represented during the American Revolution
questions.explanation:
Answer:
b) How the colonists came together to make a decision to declare independence.
Explanation:
The main idea of this passage is how the colonists agreed to declare their independence from British rule. The passage also mentions that the Declaration of Independence was written by Thomas Jefferson, but that is not the main point of the passage.

World War 1
In 1914, fighting broke out. It was the beginning of World War 1. On one side there was Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Italy. They formed an alliance called the Central Powers. France, Russia, and Britain were on the other side. These three countries were known as the Allies.
The huge Ottoman Empire joined the Central Powers. The war spread into Africa. Japan joined the Allies. A few countries remained neutral.
There were many battles, and hundreds of thousands of soldiers died. In 1917, German submarines attacked several US ships. In the same year, the United States joined the Allies and entered the war. Millions of Americans signed up for war duty.  American factories began producing rifles, blankets, boots, and trucks.
Question

questions.question:
Read the following text and answer the question at the end:
Female Reformers in the Progressive Era
(Text courtesy of crusade for the vote.org)
In the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, women joined national organizations in great numbers. The rise of the National American Woman Suffrage Association, National Association Opposed to Woman Suffrage, and National Association of Colored Women grew as part of this trend. Women of all backgrounds—rich and poor, white and black, native-born Americans and immigrants—participated in these national women’s clubs. The Woman’s Christian Temperance Movement, which aimed to make alcohol illegal, was among the most popular national women’s organizations of the period. Their movement succeeded with the start of the nationwide prohibition of alcohol in 1919.
Women became leaders in a range of social and political movements from 1890 through 1920. This period is known as the Progressive Era. Progressive reformers wanted to end political corruption, improve the lives of individuals, and increase government intervention to protect citizens.
The suffrage movement was part of this wave of Progressive Era reforms. Prominent suffragists led other progressive causes as well. Jane Addams established Chicago’s Hull House, a settlement house that educated and provided services for local immigrants. Ida B. Wells-Barnett led a campaign against the lynching of African Americans.
Question:
Is the following statement true or false?
Women in the Progressive Era campaigned for reforms that included: banning alcohol and lynching, providing services and education to immigrants, and ending corruption in government.
questions.explanation:
Answer: b)
Explanation:

True.
According to the passage, women in the Progressive Era campaigned for many causes, including banning lynching, banning alcohol, ending corruption, and providing education to immigrants.

What Was the WPA?
President Franklin D. Roosevelt created the WPA with an executive order on May 6, 1935. It was part of his New Deal plan to lift the country out of the Great Depression by reforming the financial system and restoring the economy to pre-Depression levels.
The unemployment rate in 1935 was at a staggering 20 percent. The WPA was designed to provide relief for the unemployed by providing jobs and income for millions of Americans. At its height in late 1938, more than 3.3 million Americans worked for the WPA.
The WPA – which in 1939 was renamed the Work Projects Administration – employed mostly unskilled men to carry out public works infrastructure projects. They built more than 4,000 new school buildings, erected 130 new hospitals, laid roughly 9,000 miles of storm drains and sanitary sewer lines, built 29,000 new bridges, constructed 150 new airfields, paved or repaired 280,000 miles of roads, and planted 24 million trees.
(Courtesy of History.com)

. The WPA was designed to provide entry-level jobs for the unemployed, as well as help build public infrastructure and restore the economy.

questions.question:
Read the text below and answer the questions at the bottom:
American Women in the Armed Forces in World War 2
In addition to factory work and other home front jobs, some 350,000 women joined the Armed Services, serving at home and abroad. At the urging of First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt and women’s groups, and impressed by the British use of women in service, General George Marshall supported the idea of introducing a women’s service branch into the Army.
In May 1942, Congress instituted the Women’s Auxiliary Army Corps, later upgraded to the Women’s Army Corps, which had full military status. Its members, known as WACs, worked in more than 200 non-combatant jobs stateside and in every theater of the war. By 1945, there were more than 100,000 WACs and 6,000 female officers. In the Navy, members of Women Accepted for Volunteer Emergency Service (WAVES) held the same status as naval reservists and provided support stateside.
The Coast Guard and Marine Corps soon followed suit, though in smaller numbers.
(Courtesy of History.com)
QUESTION:
Why did General Marshall support the idea of a women’s army corps? Choose the best answer.
options: because he was impressed by British women serving in the armed forces
because the president’s wife encouraged him
because the Navy had started a women’s service (the WAVES)

because of A and B above
questions.explanation:
Answer and Explanation:
The correct answer is
A
and
B.
According to the first paragraph of the passage, General Marshall was impressed by the British women serving in the armed forces. He was also encouraged by First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt (the president’s wife) and women’s groups.

questions.question:
Two writers in 2014 wrote about whether the United States should give guns to Ukraine as it fought separatists who wanted to leave Ukraine and join Russia. Read excerpts from their articles (adapted from newsela.com) and answer the question.
ARTICLE 1: An acceptable arrangement can be achieved
By John B. Quigley
Ukrainian President Petro Poroshenko is asking the U.S. for military aid. Poroshenko wants weapons to fight people in his country who want to break away and join Russia.
There is a cease-fire deal to stop the fighting in Ukraine. The deal was made between its government and the separatists. The separatists hold the major eastern cities of Donetsk and Luhansk. If the cease-fire holds to stop the fighting, the warfare that has wrecked some parts of eastern Ukraine will not continue.
Giving Ukraine weapons would risk making the situation there worse. It would come at a time when matters seem to be getting fixed. A Senate committee has called for the United States to give weapons to Ukraine’s government. But what the United States should now do is to help the cease-fire hold. There is every reason to believe that an acceptable arrangement can be achieved that will end the bloodshed in Ukraine.
ARTICLE 2: Putin won’t be stopped
By Lawrence J. Haas
Congress has an opportunity to push the United States in a more effective direction to help Ukraine defend itself against Russia. A Senate proposal would give Ukraine $350 million in military aid. It needs money and weapons to fight Russia from taking more of its land. Republican and Democratic lawmakers should vote to approve the proposal.
Russian President Vladimir Putin dreams of bringing back the Soviet Union. Putin wants to go back to the days when Russia ruled over Eastern Europe.
Putin won’t be stopped by the weak actions of the U.S. and Western Europe. So far, they’ve only put in place weak trade blocks to prevent countries and businesses from buying and selling with Russia.
In mid-September, Russian nuclear bombers flew within 63 miles of Alaska’s coast and 46 miles of Canada’s. The action forced U.S. and Canadian jets to fly out and meet them. Russia’s actions come at the same time as the country is improving its nuclear weapons with new missiles, submarines, and a new bomber. We’ll surely see more Russian attacks in Ukraine and beyond.
QUESTION
:
Which of the statements below is an opinion?
options: Ukrainian President Petro Poroshenko is asking the U.S. for military aid.
A Senate committee has called for the United States to give weapons to Ukraine's government.
There is a cease-fire deal to stop the fighting in Ukraine.
We’ll surely see more Russian attacks in Ukraine and beyond.
questions.explanation:

Explanation:
The correct answer is
“We’ll surely see more Russian attacks in Ukraine and beyond.”
This statement is an opinion because it is a prediction that is based on what the author of the article thinks might happen. The other statements are factual statements.

The National Coral Reef Monitoring Program (NCRMP)
Coral reefs provide an estimated $3.4 billion annually in total economic value to the U.S. The “Coral Reef Conservation Act of 2000” authorizes a national program that includes “monitoring [and] assessment … that benefits the understanding, sustainable use, and long-term conservation of coral reefs and coral reef ecosystems.” NOAA developed the National Coral Reef Monitoring Program (NCRMP) to:
support conservation of the United States’ coral reef ecosystems
provide an ecosystem perspective by monitoring climate and fish

questions.question:
The Taft-Hartley Act
Under the provisions of Section 14(b) of the Taft-Hartley Act of 1947, states were given the power to pass “right-to-work” laws restricting the union shop. A union shop is a workplace where all workers must belong to the union. A wildcat strike is a strike with no warning. Although organized labor worked to get Congress to repeal this section of the Act, by 2012, 23 states had passed such laws. Two points of view from the debate that followed the passage of the Taft-Hartley Act are presented below. They are from newspapers that had opposite opinions
Newspaper X said:
“The union shop is necessary and just and should not be banned. Open shops create labor-management friction that leads to dissatisfaction and wildcat strikes. Unions provide workers with a channel through which they can voice grievances and collectively bargain for wages, working conditions, and hours. Since union agreements generally apply to all workers, why should some get a free ride by receiving union benefits without paying union dues?
“Section 14(b) should also be repealed in the interest of regulating interstate commerce. No state should be allowed to enact laws that would give it a commercial advantage over another state. Why shouldn’t the government act to strengthen labor? It aids business by providing protective tariffs, subsidies, tax advantages, and research.
“The mass media have always been anti-labor; they have consistently failed to point out that the per-capita income in the right-to-work states is far below the national average.”
Newspaper Y wrote:
“If workers cannot be barred from jobs because of race or religion, they should not be barred because they do not wish to join a union. Conscientious objectors are not forced into the army; why should independent jobholders be forced into unions?
“Right-to-work laws do not give states unfair advantages. Raw materials, transportation, and markets are of prime importance in attracting industry.
“The right of the states to forbid the union shop is a valuable check on the use of union power. We feel that instead of being allowed more freedom, unions should be subject to more government control.”
QUESTION: Newspaper Y considered the right-to-work laws to be based on the same principle as laws that:
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) Protect citizens’ civil right
Explanation:
Newspaper Y compares right-to-work laws with the protection of citizens based on race, religion, and conscientious objector status. These are all civil rights issues. Newspaper Y considered right-to-work laws to be based on the same principle as laws that protect citizens’ civil rights.

People must stay angry about mass shootings
By Don Kusler
By now, it’s easy to see what will happen after Las Vegas. The horrible attack is only the latest in a number of mass shootings in the United States. The community and the country feel hurt and upset. News outlets cover the story for several days while lawmakers send their thoughts and prayers. People talk about changing gun laws.
The National Rifle Association asks for people to wait. And people do wait. Then nothing changes and the news moves on to report on more current events. All the while, the powerful gun lobby that influences lawmakers, prevents smart policies and laws on firearms.
This happens every time there is a mass shooting and it is a cycle that we must break. People who support guns always use the same excuses. The Second Amendment, personal protection, recreational use, fear of a police state, and a general call for freedom.
None of these arguments are logical.
The Second Amendment grants U.S. citizens the right to possess firearms. However, it was written in a very different time. There was no police protection, and there were no automatic weapons that could kill so many people so quickly.
The idea that people own guns for self-defense is unrealistic. Statistics show that very few gun owners are able to successfully defend themselves or others in an emergency.
Guns for recreational use, like hunting, are fine. That doesn’t mean we can’t have stricter laws on who can buy guns and the safety of those guns.
There’s also the slippery slope argument. First, the argument goes, the government will restrict guns. Then, they’ll ban them altogether. Then, what will the government ban next? People who dislike this argument say that it is important to protect our freedoms.
Nelson Mandela said that true freedom is “to live in a way that respects and enhances the freedom of others.” Gun ownership is a false freedom. It means others are not free from gun violence.
Lawmakers for the national government, as well as for the local and state governments, must act now. The leaders we vote for must be fearless and look past the next
y that respects an
d enhances the freedom of others.” Gun ownership is a false freedom.
It means others are not free from gun violence.
I am not a city boy. I grew up in the country in Texas with a gun in my hand, but there comes a time when you must think about something bigger than yourself. We must make
newscasts or elections. Doing so would be fighting for our freedoms, not against them.
QUESTION
:
What is the author’s conclusion? Choose the best answer.
options: The government must ban the use of guns.
The National Rifle Association must introduce gun controls.
The government must act to introduce stricter gun laws.
The time has come to think about other people.
questions.explanation:
Answer: c)
Explanation:
The correct answer is
“The government must act to introduce stricter gun laws.”
In the passage, the author argues that gun ownership is a “false freedom” and that stricter gun laws would help prevent mass shootings.

questions.question:
Read the following text. Then answer the question:
Migration
The history of the world is filled with stories of people migrating. Migration is the movement of people from one place to another as they seek a new home. Famine, overpopulation, limited resources, war, and religious and political persecution “push” immigrants to move to another country. Hopes for employment and a better life “pull” immigrants to new places.
Millions have migrated to North America since the 1600s. Spanish, French, English, and Dutch immigrants were the first European settlers to establish permanent colonies. They settled in lands originally populated by people from Asia. Many people from Africa were driven from their homes at this time to be enslaved to work in colonies in the Americas.
Throughout the 1800s, immigrants looking for employment came to North America from Japan, China, and southeastern Europe. In the 1970s and 1980s, Southeast Asians, Latin Americans, and Caribbeans migrated to North America. Many of these immigrants fled from war-torn countries, political persecution, and economic difficulties.
QUESTION
:
Based on the text above, which is an opinion rather than a fact about immigrants to North America?
options: Immigrants traveled long distances to find a better life.
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) Immigrants found a better life.
Explanation:
Because the others are all facts stated or implied in the passage. Whether they have found a better life is unknown.

questions.question:
The 1930s and 1940s were turbulent years in United States history. This passage considers the impact of the Great Depression and Second World War on the United States economy.
Read the passage and then answer the question.
During the administrations of Herbert Hoover and Franklin D. Roosevelt, poverty was widespread. The Great Depression had dealt a severe blow to the economic well-being of the nation. For example, the gross national product (GNP), the total value of all goods and services produced in a year, had dropped from $103 billion in 1929 to $55 billion in 1933.
Full recovery from this depression did not come until the Second World War, when United States industry went into high gear, producing war materials. To enable the Allied armies to win the war in both Europe and the Pacific, technological miracles were achieved. Employment rose as factories worked around the clock. High wages and government-controlled prices helped create a tremendous growth in family incomes. Because of the emphasis on production of heavy goods and machinery, much of the money people earned went into savings. Measured in dollars of constant purchasing power, or what economists call “real income,” average yearly take-home pay of families grew to about $800 from 1941 to 1946, an increase of about $160 per year.
Dire predictions about mass unemployment after the war proved wrong. In the peacetime economy, industry flourished as price controls were removed and manufacturers scrambled to meet the huge demand for consumer goods. There were recessions during the twenty years after the war, but they were minor economic ripples compared with previous national depressions.
QUESTION
:
Judging from the way GNP statistics are used in this passage, it can be concluded that one of the primary purposes of the GNP figures is to analyze what?
options: The effects of government regulations on business
questions.explanation:
Answer:
c) Economic trends
.
Explanation:
According to the passage, the GNP measures the total value of all goods produced in a year. This data shows the state of the economy over a period of time.

questions.question:
This excerpt is from the “Declaration of Sentiments” presented to the Seneca Falls Convention by Elizabeth Cady Stanton in 1848.
“We hold these truths to be self-evident: that all men and women are created equal; that they are endowed by their Creator with certain inalienable rights; that among these are life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness; that to secure these rights governments are instituted, deriving their just powers from the consent of the governed. Whenever any form of Government becomes destructive of these ends, it is the right of those who suffer from it to refuse allegiance to it, and to insist upon the institution of a new government …”
QUESTION:
What concept is the main idea of this excerpt?
questions.explanation:
Answer: b)
Explanation:
The main idea of this excerpt is the idea of natural rights. These natural rights (“life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness”) are described as “inalienable”, meaning they cannot be taken away.

questions.question:
Read this passage about the 17th Amendment. Then answer the question.
“In 1787, delegates to the Constitutional Convention decided to give state legislatures the power to elect U.S. senators. The purpose was to ensure that the interests of the states were represented in that national legislature. However, some argued that the people should directly elect their senators. They thought the interests of the states would be preserved because the people were the source of all government power.
The first of nearly 300 congressional resolutions calling for direct election of senators came in 1826. Over the next 85
years, an amendment to directly elect U.S. senators was debated extensively. Finally, in 1913, the 17th Amendment, which allowed for the direct election of senators, was ratified.”
QUESTION
:  What does the word convention mean in the passage?
questions.explanation:
Answer: d)
Explanation:
In this passage, convention refers to the Constitutional Convention, which was the
formal assembly
of delegates that decided to give state legislatures the power to elect U.S. Senators in 1787.

questions.question:
Read these paragraphs about a proposed Bill of Rights written by Alexander Hamilton and James Madison. Then answer the question.
Hamilton’s Essay
Not only is a bill of rights unnecessary, I am sure that in the proposed constitution it would even be dangerous. Why declare that things will not be done when there is no power to do them? Why assert that certain rights are protected when the government has no power to violate those rights? Why state that there is freedom of the press when the government is not given power that can be used to violate freedom of the press? It would only provide an excuse for power-hungry men to claim such a power.
Madison’s Letter
I have always favored a bill of rights, so long as it does not imply that the government has powers it is not meant to have. At the same time, I do not think the absence of a bill of rights is a major defect. The real threat to individual rights is not the government, but a strong-willed majority of the people. Nevertheless, the threat may occasionally come from the government, in which case a bill of rights will be essential. It is a sad truth that freedom is endangered whether the government has too much or too little power, and finding the thin line between the extremes is not easy.
QUESTION
: Which of the writers would disagree with the following statement?
A bill of rights is necessary to protect people against possible abuse of power.
questions.explanation:
Answer: a)
Explanation:
Hamilton’s essay argues that a bill or rights is unnecessary and even dangerous.

These greenhouse gas emissions have increased the greenhouse effect and caused Earth’s surface temperature to rise. The primary human activity affecting the amount and rate of climate change is greenhouse gas emissions from the burning of fossil fuels. …
Human activities currently release over 30 billion tons of CO2 into the atmosphere every year. The resultant build-up of CO2 in the atmosphere is like a tub filling with water, where more water flows from the faucet than the drain can take away.

questions.explanation:
Answer: b)
